findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows attacker-controlled negative slice
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result() explicitly allows cursor.offset < 0 when enable_advanced_features is true and slices queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise AssertionError, and Python slicing with negative start wraps from the end. An unauthenticated cursor string from the query param therefore controls DB slicing beyond normal bounds. The comment claiming Django handles it automatically and permissions at queryset level make it safe is false. Consequence is DoS (500s) and bypass of intended pagination bounds.

findings.title: Audit-log endpoint exposes advanced paginator on weak gate
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py the endpoint switches to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True when request.GET optimized_pagination==true and request.user.is_superuser or member.has_global_access. has_global_access is true for many org admins, not just superusers, so any such user can trigger the negative-offset path by crafting a cursor. The queryset remains filtered but pagination logic is now attacker-influenced. Consequence is privilege-adjacent attack surface for the DoS/bounds issue in the paginator.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator used with datetime ordering will crash
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() does int(math.floor(value)) assuming a numeric key, identical to Paginator. The caller in organization_auditlogs.py uses order_by=-datetime, so value is a datetime object. math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError on every page that builds a cursor. Consequence is the optimized audit-log path is broken and returns 500s.

findings.title: Mandatory end_timestamp_precise access crashes consumer on missing field
findings.body: In src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py process_batch() does val[end_timestamp_precise] with direct key access. Any span event without that field, malformed Relay output, or schema evolution raises KeyError inside the Arroyo batch processor. Because the exception occurs after Kafka receipt but before offset commit, the same message will be retried and can stall the spans consumer. Consequence is poison-pill crash loop and pipeline backlog. It should use .get with fallback or validation.

findings.title: Silent span eviction with zpopmin causes unmonitored data loss
findings.body: In src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua after merging sets the script does if span_count>1000 then zpopmin(set_key, span_count-1000). Combined with src/sentry/spans/buffer.py removing the max_segment_spans skip-and-log check in _load_segment_data, oversized segments are no longer skipped with metrics/logs but silently truncated to 1000 members, dropping earliest spans by score. Consequence is permanent loss of span data in large traces with no alert, and ZUNIONSTORE default SUM aggregate also corrupts scores for duplicate members, breaking timestamp ordering.

findings.title: BasePaginator prev-path still passes negative offset to queryset
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result() was changed to start_offset = max(0,offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. When cursor.is_prev is true a negative offset is passed directly to queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django raises AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported for such slices. Consequence is a crafted prev cursor causes 500 errors and breaks reverse pagination.
